# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

 const data = input instanceof Uint8Array ? input : new Uint8Array(input);

 if (status < 0x80) return null; // no running status

  case 0x80: if(data.length<i+3) return null; return {type:'noteoff',channel,note:data[i+1],velocity:data[i+2],number:data[i+1],value:data[i+2],raw:[...data]};
  case 0x90: {
    const note=data[i+1], velocity=data[i+2];
    return {type: velocity===0?'noteoff':'noteon', channel, note, velocity, number:note, value:velocity, raw:[...data], pressed: velocity>0};
  }

```js
export function estimateBpm(buffer) {
 const sr=buffer.sampleRate; const ch=buffer.getChannelData(0);
 const maxSamples=Math.min(ch.length, sr*60);
 const hop=Math.max(64, Math.round(sr*0.01));
 const frames=Math.floor((maxSamples-hop)/hop);
 const energy=new Float32Array(frames);
 for i: sum squares across hop? Use abs sum with stride 2 for speed.
 const onset=new Float32Array(frames);
 let mean=0;
 for i=1..: onset[i]=Math.max(0, Math.log(1+energy[i]*1000)-Math.log(1+energy[i-1]*1000)); mean += onset[i];
 mean/=frames;
 // autocorr lags frames 30..100 (for 60-200bpm at 100fps)
 let best={bpm:0,score:0};
 for (lag=30; lag<=100; lag++) {
   let s=0, e1=0,e2=0;
   for (i=lag;i<frames;i++){ const a=onset[i]-mean,b=onset[i-lag]-mean; s+=a*b; e1+=a*a; e2+=b*b;}
   const corr = s/Math.sqrt(e1*e2+1e-9);
   // prior favor 100-140
   const bpm=60/(lag*0.01);
   const prior = Math.exp(-Math.pow(Math.log(bpm/120),2)/0.12);
   const score=corr*prior;
   ...
 }
 let bpm=best.bpm;
 while(bpm<80) bpm*=2; while(bpm>160) bpm/=2;
 return {bpm: Math.round(bpm*10)/10, confidence: Math.max(0,best.score)};
}
```

import test from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { decodeRelative, describeMidiMessage, formatBinding, parseMidiMessage } from '../js/midi-core.js'

test('parses note on and note off, including velocity-zero note off', () => {
  const on = parseMidiMessage(new Uint8Array([0x90, 60, 100]))
  assert.equal(on.type, 'noteon')
  assert.equal(on.channel, 0)
  assert.equal(on.note, 60)
  assert.equal(on.velocity, 100)
  assert.equal(on.pressed, true)

  const off = parseMidiMessage([0x80, 60, 0])
  assert.equal(off.type, 'noteoff')
  assert.equal(off.note, 60)

  const zero = parseMidiMessage([0x93, 61, 0])
  assert.equal(zero.type, 'noteoff')
  assert.equal(zero.channel, 3)
})

test('parses CC, pitch bend, aftertouch, program and sysex', () => {
  const cc = parseMidiMessage([0xb2, 33, 64])
  assert.equal(cc.type, 'cc')
  assert.equal(cc.controller, 33)
  assert.equal(cc.value, 64)
  assert.equal(cc.channel, 2)

  const bend = parseMidiMessage([0xe0, 0x00, 0x40])
  assert.equal(bend.type, 'pitchbend')
  assert.equal(bend.value, 0)
  const bendUp = parseMidiMessage([0xe1, 0x7f, 0x7f])
  assert.equal(bendUp.type, 'pitchbend')
  assert.ok(bendUp.unit > 0.99)

  assert.equal(parseMidiMessage([0xd0, 55]).type, 'channelpressure')
  assert.equal(parseMidiMessage([0xc0, 7]).type, 'program')
  assert.equal(parseMidiMessage([0xf0, 1, 2, 0xf7]).type, 'sysex')
  assert.equal(parseMidiMessage([0x01, 2, 3]), null)
  assert.equal(parseMidiMessage([]), null)
})

test('decodes relative jog encoders in every supported mode', () => {
  // two's complement / auto
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(1, 'auto'), 1)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(5, 'auto'), 5)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(127, 'auto'), -1)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(120, 'auto'), -8)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(64, 'auto'), 0)

  // offset
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(64, 'offset'), 0)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(70, 'offset'), 6)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(58, 'offset'), -6)

  // signed bit
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(1, 'signed'), 1)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(64, 'signed'), 0)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(127, 'signed'), -1)

  // absolute delta wraps around the 7-bit range
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(10, 'absolute', 5), 5)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(120, 'absolute', 5), -13)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(5, 'absolute', 120), 13)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(50, 'absolute', null), 0)

  // linear absolute
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(70, 'absolute0', 60), 10)
  assert.equal(decodeRelative(10, 'absolute0', 60), -50)
})

test('formats bindings and monitor strings', () => {
  assert.equal(formatBinding({ type: 'cc', channel: 0, number: 33 }), 'CH 1 · CC 33')
  assert.equal(formatBinding({ type: 'note', channel: 2, number: 54 }), 'CH 3 · NOTE 54')
  assert.equal(formatBinding({ type: 'pitchbend', channel: 0, number: 0 }), 'CH 1 · PITCH BEND')
  assert.equal(formatBinding(null), '—')
  assert.match(describeMidiMessage({ channel: 0, type: 'cc', controller: 7, value: 127 }), /CC 7/)
})

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete browser DJ app like Algoriddim djay Pro with working jog-wheel scratching, user MP3 import, Web MIDI controller support, message parsing, capacitive vs non-touch platter behavior, and relative rotation mapping to playback speed/scrubbing.

## Requirements
- Handle MIDI control messages (notes, CC, pitch bend, etc.).
- Differentiate touch-sensitive/capacitive platters from non-touch platters.
- Map relative jog rotation to audio playback rate and scrubbing, including reverse.
- Support user MP3 files and be immediately playable.
- Build complete app without asking clarifying questions; note assumptions when done.

## Decisions
- Vanilla ES modules + static HTML/CSS, no build step (repo runtime expects `index.html`).
- AudioWorklet-based read-head engine (`deck-processor.js`) instead of `AudioBufferSourceNode`, because it supports negative playback rates for real scratching.
- Four procedurally generated demo tracks so the app works without user files.
- MIDI Learn plus guided auto-map wizard instead of unreliable hardcoded controller profiles.
- Capacitive detection is derived from whether a `touch` note binding exists.
- Non-touch platters auto-grab on rotation; capacitive platters scratch while touched and pitch-nudge when untouched (Auto mode, configurable).
- Relative jog default decode: 7-bit two's complement with `64 => 0`, plus offset/signed/absolute modes.
- Added virtual MIDI controller for users/testers without hardware; it feeds the same parser.
- Persistence via `localStorage` for MIDI mappings, platter settings, and hot cues.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project implementation files created: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `js/app.js` (~1,900 lines), `js/audio-engine.js`, `js/deck-processor.js`, `js/midi.js`, `js/midi-core.js`, `js/analysis.js`, `js/demo-tracks.js`.
- Node unit tests added and passing: `tests/midi-core.test.mjs`, `tests/analysis.test.mjs` (7/7 pass).
- `node --check` passes for all JS modules.
- Static server started in tmux session `scratchlab` on port 3002; `curl` returns HTTP 200.
- Automated Playwright verification script written at `/tmp/verify-scratchlab.mjs`; debug script at `/tmp/debug-scratchlab.mjs`.
- Playwright run exposed a startup bug; error identified:
  - `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'classList') at updateMidiStatus (js/app.js:1140:20)`
  - Also a 404 resource error (likely favicon, not confirmed).
- Startup currently fails before `window.scratchlab.ready` becomes true; boot overlay shows `AUDIO ENGINE FAILED`.

### Active
- Fix `updateMidiStatus` referencing `ui.virtualToggle`, which was never added to the `ui` object in `app.js`.
- Then rerun Playwright desktop/mobile verification, inspect screenshots, and iterate on layout/audio behavior.

### Blocked
- None technically; browser verification cannot proceed until the `ui.virtualToggle` reference is fixed.

## Next Move
1. Add `virtualToggle: $('#virtualToggle')` (and check other `ui.*` refs such as `ui.midiDot`, `ui.enableMidi`) to the `ui` object in `js/app.js`.
2. Search `js/app.js` for all `ui.<name>` usages and ensure every one exists in the `ui` declaration; also check for other runtime nulls.
3. Rerun `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` and `node --check js/app.js`.
4. Rerun `DISPLAY=:0 node /tmp/verify-scratchlab.mjs`; inspect `/tmp/scratchlab-shots/*.png`.
5. Validate: play deck A advances position; MIDI CC 33 relative jog moves/scrubs audio; touch note 54 toggles capacitive behavior; crossfader CC works; virtual controller works; no console errors.
6. Check mobile layout at 390×844 for horizontal overflow and usable controls.
7. Iterate CSS/UI for visual polish and fix any audio/scratch behavior issues.
8. Update `README.md` with app description/run instructions if time permits, and give final summary with assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/app.js`: main UI orchestration, deck logic, MIDI controls, wizard, animation, boot; current bug at `updateMidiStatus` line ~1140.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: full DOM structure/IDs referenced by app.js.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: full responsive visual design; virtual dock z-index raised to 96.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/midi.js`: MIDI manager, mappings, capture, virtual controller, learn; tempo pitch-bend mapping patched.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/midi-core.js`: MIDI parser and relative decoder; `64 => 0` fix applied.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio-engine.js`: Web Audio graph, deck transport, EQ/filter/echo/crossfader.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/deck-processor.js`: AudioWorklet signed-rate scratch engine.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/analysis.js`: waveform peaks, BPM estimate, time formatting.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/demo-tracks.js`: procedural demo tracks.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/midi-core.test.mjs`: passing MIDI/relative decoder tests.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/analysis.test.mjs`: passing BPM/peaks tests.
- `/tmp/verify-scratchlab.mjs`: Playwright desktop/mobile verification and screenshots.
- `/tmp/debug-scratchlab.mjs`: console/pageerror capture helper.
- `/tmp/scratchlab-server.log`: server log.
- `/tmp/scratchlab-shots/`: screenshots (debug.png currently captured).

## Important Context
- Run tests with: `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`.
- Server is running in tmux session `scratchlab`: `PORT=3002 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"` from project root.
- Playwright launch config: `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json`; set `DISPLAY=:0`.
- Exact current startup error: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'classList') at updateMidiStatus (http://localhost:3002/js/app.js:1140:20) at setupMidi (js/app.js:1238:3) at init (js/app.js:1867:5)`.
- Root cause: `ui.virtualToggle` is not defined, though `#virtualToggle` exists in `index.html` and is used directly in `setupVirtualController` as `$('#virtualToggle')`.
- UI IDs use deck suffix A/B (`playA`, `waveZoomB`, etc.); `deckRefs()` maps them.
- Debug API: `window.scratchlab` with `snapshot()`, `loadDemo(deck,index)`, `play`, `pause`, `toggle`, `jog(id,delta)`, `touch(id,down)`, `midiRaw(bytes)`, `sendVirtual(bytes)`, `bind(target,binding)`, `midi`, `audio`.
- Mapping targets include `deckA.jog`, `deckA.touch`, `deckA.play`, `deckA.cue`, `deckA.sync`, `deckA.tempo`, `deckA.volume`, `deckA.filter`, `deckA.eqHigh/Mid/Low`, `deckA.pad1..4`, same for `deckB`, plus `mixer.crossfader`, `mixer.master`.
- Default virtual mapping uses channel 15: Deck A jog CC100, touch note60, play note70; Deck B jog CC101, touch note61, play note71; crossfader CC7.
- Audio context may start suspended; first pointer/key gesture resumes it. Deck A/B are loaded with demo tracks 1 and 2, paused.
- Screenshot capture can click the first button exactly labeled `Start`/`Play`; deck play buttons are icon-only with aria-label `Play deck A/B`, so no auto-start.
- Generated demo tracks: 16 bars, 4 tracks, BPMs 124/128/118/132, memory ~4 stereo buffers; boot generation timing still unmeasured.
- CSS uses `color-mix()` and `writing-mode: vertical-lr` vertical range sliders; verify in the actual Chromium screenshot.

# ScratchLab — Browser DJ Booth

A two-deck browser DJ app with a real signed-rate scratch engine, Web MIDI controller support, capacitive platter detection, and drag-and-drop MP3 import. No build step, no uploads — audio stays on the device.

## Run it

```bash
# from this repository root
python3 -m http.server 3002
# or use the project start script
./start.sh
```

Open <http://localhost:3002>. Chrome or Edge is recommended for Web MIDI. Click anywhere once (or the audio chip) to resume the audio context.

## Highlights

- **Real jog-wheel scratching** — an AudioWorklet moves an interpolated read-head at signed rates, so reverse scratches, pitch bends, and touch-to-scratch feel immediate. A plain `AudioBufferSourceNode` cannot play backwards reliably.
- **Import your own MP3s** — use **IMPORT MP3** or drag audio files onto the page. Files are decoded locally, analysed for BPM, rendered in the library, and loaded to a deck instantly.
- **Web MIDI input** — notes, CCs, pitch bend, aftertouch, program changes, and clock/sysex are parsed. A live monitor shows every incoming message and decoded jog delta.
- **Capacitive vs non-touch platters** — mapping a touch note marks the deck `CAPACITIVE`. In **AUTO** mode, capacitive decks scratch only while touched and pitch-nudge when released; non-touch decks auto-grab on rotation and release after the wheel stops.
- **Relative decoder modes** — 7-bit two's complement (`64 = 0`), offset, signed-bit, and absolute delta modes, plus adjustable ticks-per-revolution and sensitivity.
- **MIDI Learn and guided auto-map** — bind any control from MIDI Setup, or run the wizard and move each control once.
- **Virtual MIDI controller** — test the full MIDI path without hardware; it feeds the same parser as a physical controller.
- **Two full decks** — play/cue, sync, loops, four hot cues, tempo, 3-band EQ, filter, echo, channel faders, crossfader, master volume, waveforms, and VU meters.
- **Four demo tracks** — procedurally generated so the app is playable before importing anything.

## Default virtual-controller mapping

| Control | Deck A | Deck B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jog (relative CC) | CH 16 · CC 100 | CH 16 · CC 101 |
| Touch sensor (note) | CH 16 · Note 60 | CH 16 · Note 61 |
| Play | CH 16 · Note 70 | CH 16 · Note 71 |
| Cue | CH 16 · Note 72 | CH 16 · Note 73 |
| Hot cues 1–4 | Notes 80–83 | Notes 84–87 |

Crossfader: **CH 16 · CC 7**.

## Keyboard shortcuts

- `Space` / `A` — play or pause Deck A
- `L` — play or pause Deck B
- `S` / `;` — cue Deck A / Deck B
- `Q` / `E` — scratch Deck A backwards / forwards
- `U` / `O` — scratch Deck B backwards / forwards
- `←` / `→` — move the crossfader
- `Esc` — close the topmost panel

## Tests

```bash
node --test tests/*.test.mjs
```

The tests cover MIDI parsing, relative-jog decoding modes, BPM estimation, waveform peaks, and display formatting.

## Notes and assumptions

- MP3/audio decoding uses the browser's `decodeAudioData`; support follows the browser codec list.
- MIDI Learn is used instead of hardcoded controller profiles because jog CCs, touch notes, and channels vary between manufacturers.
- The default relative encoding is 7-bit two's complement (`64 = 0`). If your wheel turns the wrong way or feels too sensitive, change **Encoder type**, **Ticks per revolution**, or **Scratch sensitivity** in MIDI Setup.
- Beat detection is best-effort analysis for imported files; manually verified BPMs are not required for scratching or playback.
- MIDI mappings, platter settings, and hot cues persist in `localStorage`.

<!-- omgithub:readme:start -->

## ScratchLab is built and verified

A complete two-deck browser DJ app is running at **http://localhost:3002** (server started with `./start.sh`).

### What works

- **Real jog-wheel scratching** via an AudioWorklet read-head engine — forward, reverse, touch-grab, and pitch nudge. Verified with actual reverse playback (`rate -2.57`) and audio signal output.
- **User MP3 import** through **IMPORT MP3** or drag-and-drop. Confirmed with a real MP3: decoded, analysed, added to the library, loaded, and played immediately.
- **Web MIDI support** — notes, CC, pitch bend, aftertouch, sysex, and clock parsing, live monitor, MIDI Learn, and a guided 7-step auto-map wizard.
- **Capacitive vs non-touch platters**:
  - A mapped touch sensor marks the deck **CAPACITIVE**.
  - Touch → scratch; release → resume.
  - No touch mapping → rotation auto-grabs and scratches, then releases.
  - Verified all modes in-browser.
- **Relative rotation decoding** — 7-bit two's complement (`64 = 0`), offset, signed-bit, and absolute modes, plus ticks-per-revolution and sensitivity controls.
- **Full deck/mixer controls** — play, cue, sync, loops, 4 hot cues, tempo, 3-band EQ, filter, echo, channel faders, crossfader, master volume, waveforms, VU meters, four demo tracks.
- **Virtual MIDI controller** for testing without hardware; it feeds the same parser.
- **Persistence** of mappings, platter settings, and hot cues via `localStorage`.

### Verification

- `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` → **9/9 passing**
- Desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844: **zero console/page errors**, no horizontal overflow
- Auto-map wizard completed end-to-end with simulated MIDI
- MIDI settings persisted across reload
- Real MP3 import and short-track end/restart behavior confirmed

### Key files

- `index.html`, `styles.css`
- `js/app.js` — UI, decks, scratch logic, mapping wizard
- `js/audio-engine.js`, `js/deck-processor.js` — signed-rate AudioWorklet engine
- `js/midi.js`, `js/midi-core.js` — MIDI parsing, decoding, learn, virtual controller
- `js/analysis.js`, `js/demo-tracks.js`
- `tests/` — 9 tests
- `README.md` — run instructions, controls, mappings, assumptions

### Assumptions

- Capacitive detection is derived from whether a **Touch sensor** binding exists for that deck.
- Default relative encoding is **7-bit two's complement (`64 = 0`)**, since controller jog formats vary.
- MIDI Learn/auto-map is used instead of hardcoded controller profiles.
- Web MIDI requires Chrome/Edge on localhost or HTTPS.
- Imported BPM is only shown when analysis confidence is reasonably high.
